Hi Karthik —

Attached is Nimbus's redline to Exhibit B (Pricing Schedule) and a provisional rate matrix for the first 12 months. High level: we are proposing a temporary cushion on the minimum fee (floor) of 20% for Q1–Q2 while we onboard, and a quarterly true-up to handle early adoption variance.

Key asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood can accept a provisional rate table that allows for a 20% floor cushion for the first two quarters.
- Add quarterly true-up language with a short form of the metrics to be used (we put a suggested clause in the redline).
- Confirm cap on monthly overage rates (we left the existing cap but want confirmation that any cap will not be lowered during the first 12 months).

We've included an editable spreadsheet for the provisional rates and a tracked redline (Nimbus_Pricing_Redline_v3.docx, Provisional_Rate_Matrix.xlsx).

Thanks Erin — received, and appreciate the clarity in the spreadsheet. Two quick notes from product/ops perspective before we engage legal:

1) "Provisional rate matrix" — can you confirm whether the matrix is intended to be a binding schedule (i.e., Exhibit B replaces current schedule) or a transient appendix that will be superseded by the first true-up? We want to ensure routing & billing treat provisional rows differently to avoid automated alerts.

2) The 20% floor cushion for Q1–Q2: ops can support a temporary waiver on the minimum but we typically gate these to an onboarding SLA (e.g., <30 days to hit baseline). Can you share the onboarding milestones Nimbus expects to use as triggers?

I'll loop in Marissa and Ben to give commercial counterpoints; Laura, can you take a first pass on the redline (Exhibit B) and flag any language that would leave us exposed on revenue recognition or indefinite price-lock risk?

I attached a short internal note to capture our talking points. Suggest we do a 30-min call Tues to align and then exchange a single consolidated counter.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference

Karthik — quick clarifications inline:

On Mon, Jul 12, 2027 at 11:02 AM karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> "Provisional rate matrix" — can you confirm whether the matrix is intended to be a binding schedule...

Good question. Nimbus intends the matrix to be binding for billing during the provisional period (we propose Q1–Q2) and then subject to an agreed true-up at the end of Q2 — i.e., the provisional rows will remain in the live billing sheet and then be replaced by the post-true-up schedule.

On onboarding triggers: attached is a simple list of milestones (onboarding_milestones.txt) — highlights: completion of integration test plan, ingestion of first 100k tokens, and training of 2 internal workflows. We expect the 20% floor cushion to apply until the second true-up settles.

If that helps, the matrix is intentionally conservative on the upside and is meant to protect Nimbus from front-loaded usage during ramp.

Erin

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Shaw <erin.shaw@nimbushealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redline + provisional rate matrix

Erin — thanks for the extra color and the milestones doc. Commercial thoughts below (keeping it practical so we can converge to a single counter):

- Provisional vs binding: we can accept a "provisional binding" table that lives as an appendix for the first two quarters with a mandatory true-up at the end of Q2 that reconciles to actuals. We prefer the language to be explicit that the provisional table is superseded by the post-true-up schedule.

- Floor cushion: our preference is a capped cushion rather than an open %. Suggest 12% for Q1 and 8% for Q2 (sliding down) rather than a flat 20% so incentives are better aligned.

- Quarterly vs annual true-up: quarterly true-ups add operational overhead and invoicing churn. We are open to a mid-year reconciliation (end of Q2 only) with an optional interim report each quarter — this reduces billing churn but keeps transparency.

- Cap protection: we can confirm that the current cap remains but need a carve-out that prevents downward movement of the cap mid-contract (we'll propose a non-reduction clause for 12 months).

Action items we propose:
1) Redwood to produce a countersheet (clean + tracked) with: revised cushion (12%/8%), single mid-year true-up clause, and explicit override language for the provisional appendix.
2) Legal (Laura) to produce one redlined clause addressing termination/renegotiation risk and revenue recognition exposure.
3) Schedule 30-min alignment call Weds 10am PT if that works for your team.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Erin / Nimbus legal —

Thanks for the materials. I've attached a redline of Exhibit B and the provisional matrix wording with suggested edits (Exhibit_B_Rate_Matrix_Redline.docx). High-level legal points we changed or added:

- Defined "Provisional Period" explicitly as "the first two (2) full billing quarters following go-live" and tied the provisional rows to the provisional appendix so they are not treated as permanent pricing.
- Modified the cushion to read as a capped variance ("up to 12% in Q1 and up to 8% in Q2") rather than an unconditional 20% floor increase.
- Replaced quarterly mandatory true-up with a mandatory mid-year reconciliation (end of Q2) with optional interim reporting each quarter. This preserves Nimbus's reconciliation request while limiting billing churn.
- Inserted a non-reduction warranty for the cap for 12 months and a clause that any permanent price adjustments require mutual written agreement.
- Added a short revenue recognition carve-out to avoid language that would lock in discounted guaranteed minimums for accounting purposes beyond the provisional period.

If you can accept the redline items above, we will prepare a clean countersheet and a short summary for your CFO and procurement team. Otherwise please flag any provisions you cannot accept and we can escalate to a short exec call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
